complexity_ledger.narrative: MF-036 makes the complexity check ADVISORY. A probe built a plain 5-variable, 10-command god-object CLI (recorded under results/probe/GodObjectCli.tla) and ran `analyze complexity`; it HARD-FAILED with "component C1 is touched by 10 actions, exceeding max_component_actions 8" (exit 1). Any program with more than eight commands over shared state failed the same way -- i.e. most real programs. Per owner direction 2026-07-20 and references/architecture_tractability.md ("Advisory, Not Blocking"), complexity is a scanner, not a gate. What changed (scripts only, zero TLA delta): (1) Every complexity threshold breach -- state-space bound, component variables, component actions, and the TLC distinct-states check -- is now an advisory WARNING that names the component/variable/action and RECOMMENDS a concrete move (e.g. "split the densest state <v> into its own component"). `analyze complexity` exits 0 whenever it can analyze the model; it exits nonzero ONLY when it CANNOT analyze it (the MF-030 fail-closed on an unresolved EXTENDS/INSTANCE hierarchy). "I could not measure this" stays an error; "this is complex" is now a finding. (2) Case generation no longer refuses above threshold. `enforce_complexity_gate` became `advise_complexity`: it prints the warnings and proceeds. The `--allow-over-budget` override was removed entirely -- there is no gate left to override. (3) Frame-condition accuracy fix: `v' = v` (the written-out form of UNCHANGED) was counted as a read AND a write, so every variable an action leaves alone showed as coupled to it. It is now stripped. On the GodObjectCli probe this drops the over-reported god-state from all five variables at 10/10 to the real coupling (only the shared `status` at 10/10; the four domain vars at 3/3/2/2), and the R/W interaction graph de-densifies from the complete graph (10 edges) to a star (4 edges). Evidence integrity is untouched: no case is dropped, no effect gap suppressed, no finding silenced. The kill-test mutant inv-SpecUnitTestsRequireAnalyzedGate was kept (its `find` pattern retargeted to the renamed variable) so that bypassing the scan -- which would silence the warnings -- is still a killable breach. The corpus case caps (corpus_diagnostics.py) and the faithfulness oracles remain as they were; un-gating those is out of this ticket's scope (MF-033 and later). Acceptance proof (results/): the probe model now emits the exact "C1 touched by 10 actions" finding as a WARNING with a recommendation and exits 0 (probe/analyze-complexity-after.txt); this repository's own model, which previously failed "C1 touched by 14 actions", now emits the same warning and promotes cleanly (repo-model-analyze-complexity-after.txt). Delta vs MF-030 is zero: bound 699,840, distinct 231,621, depth 25 (tlc.txt). Retention oracles (kill_rate/effect_conformance/external_coverage) were not re-run because the model is byte-identical to MF-030; behavior retention is witnessed by the identical TLC run rather than by a fresh oracle pass, and no complexity decrease is claimed that would require them.

refinement.detail: Zero-delta ticket. No complexity reduction was sought or made: this is a scripts-only change (analyze_complexity.py, generate_cases_from_tlc_dump.py, references/modular_fuzzing.md) that converts the complexity check from a hard gate into advisory warnings. The TLA+ model is byte-identical to MF-030 and TLC reports the same 231,621 distinct states / depth 25 (bound 699,840 unchanged). The recursive-refinement search for a further architectural reduction found none applicable, because the ticket's objective was to STOP the tooling from blocking promotion on complexity, not to reduce complexity. The one measurement-accuracy correction -- the v'=v frame-condition R/W fix -- reduces over-reported coupling in the scanner but does not change this model's own bound or reachable-state count (the model uses UNCHANGED tuples, which were already stripped; the fix matters for models that write explicit frame conditions, e.g. the recorded GodObjectCli probe).

ticket.objective: GOVERNING REFRAME (owner direction 2026-07-20), pulled to the front of the remaining work. A probe measured what the complexity gate does to ordinary programs: a 5-variable 10-command model, an unremarkable CLI over shared state, HARD-FAILED promotion because component C1 is touched by 10 actions exceeding the cap of 8. Any program with more than eight commands over shared state fails, which is most real programs, so as a hard gate the complexity metric fails in nearly every user project instead of helping. Complexity is a SCANNER, not a gate: it produces metrics, warnings and recommendations and tells the agent where to refactor, and it NEVER blocks promotion. Remove every complexity hard-fail -- analyze complexity exit-nonzero-to-block, case generation refusing above-gate, the component-size and bound checks that exit 1 -- and convert each to a warning that names what and where and recommends a move. Also fix the scanner-accuracy bug the probe found: v-prime-equals-v frame conditions are counted as touched, over-reporting coupling so every UNCHANGED variable shows as touched by every action. Keep the good scanner content that already exists: dimension table, state-space bound, R/W matrix, modularity score, dense-row god-state detection, suggested moves. What does NOT change is evidence integrity -- no dropping cases, no suppressing effect gaps, no silencing findings, because a scanner fed doctored input is worthless. See references/architecture_tractability.md Advisory Not Blocking. This resolves the everyone-fails-to-promote risk at its root.
ticket.title: Make complexity advisory: warnings and recommendations, never blocks promotion
